audience: Ethically-minded urban commuters who want a practical, low-maintenance, upright bike that rides comfortably in all weather, stands out at the bike rack, and reflects their values — sustainable, hand-built, and tied to a social mission.

positioning.title: The commuter bike that doesn't look like every other commuter bike.
positioning.lede: Upright, comfortable geometry with mounts for racks, mudguards and lights — hand-built by you from fast-growing bamboo and flax instead of carbon. A bike that turns heads at the rack, soaks up potholes, and carries a sustainability and social story no off-the-shelf frame can match.

who_for.title: The all-weather commuter
who_for.body: Rides daily, rain or shine. Wants mudguard and rack mounts, a sealed weatherproof frame, and reliability with minimal fuss.

who_for.title: The values-led rider
who_for.body: Chooses bamboo and flax over carbon for the lower footprint — and because every kit funds a place on our prison build programme.

who_for.title: The stand-out commuter
who_for.body: Tired of riding past hundreds of identical bikes. Wants one that starts conversations at the rack — and is distinctive enough to deter the casual thief.

faq.q: Can I really ride it in the rain every day?
faq.a: Yes. Finished frames are sealed with a weatherproof epoxy lacquer. Dry your bike after wet rides and store it indoors, and it'll last 8–12 years — many of our 2012 builds are still ridden daily.

faq.q: How much maintenance does a bamboo commuter need?
faq.a: Very little. Build it single-speed and there's almost nothing to service — no derailleur to adjust. Keep the chain clean, dry the frame after wet rides, and inspect the joints once a year. That's it.

faq.q: Will it handle hills and city traffic?
faq.a: The frame is single-speed or hub-gear ready, so you can spec gearing to suit your route and hills. The upright geometry gives you excellent visibility in traffic, and it fits standard racks, mudguards and lights.

faq.q: Is it strong and secure enough for daily city use?
faq.a: Around 28,000 PSI tensile strength — comparable to mild steel but lighter — with under a 1% failure rate across 4,000+ builds since 2012, independently tested with Swansea University. And because no two bamboo frames look alike, yours is far harder for a thief to pass off than a generic bike.

faq.q: Can I get it through Cycle to Work?
faq.a: Yes. Frame kits from £375 are eligible for standard Cycle to Work schemes — UK employees typically save 25–39% through salary sacrifice. We accept Cyclescheme, Cycle Solutions, Evans and Halfords.
